sentences: I measure the diameter of each marked tree at breast height and record the numbers in my field notebook.
I check the soil moisture sensors in the northwest stand every Monday morning before the crew arrives.
I mark the trees selected for thinning with blue paint on the south side of the trunk.
I plant two hundred Douglas fir seedlings along the cut block edge and water each one.
I prune the lower branches of the remaining trees to improve access and reduce fire risk.
I count the growth rings on a core sample taken from a fallen hemlock to estimate its age.
I inspect the bark of lodgepole pines for signs of beetle infestation and note the affected sections.
I maintain the firebreaks by clearing brush and fallen limbs along the western boundary of the property.
I record the canopy cover percentage at ten random points using a densiometer and a clipboard.
I check the boundary markers along the north line and replace any that are missing or damaged.
I fell a mature spruce with a chainsaw and limb it before skidding the log to the landing.
I skid the cut logs to the landing with a small tractor and stack them by species.
I apply herbicide to the invasive buckthorn sprouts along the access road and mark the treated area.
I collect cones from the best black spruce trees and store them in burlap sacks for later extraction.
I measure the height of sample trees using a clinometer and a hundred-foot tape.
I update the GIS stand maps with the new harvest boundaries and upload the shapefiles to the server.
I check the weather station data each morning for rainfall and wind speed before planning the day's work.
I maintain the forest roads by grading the surface and clearing culverts to prevent erosion.
I take an inventory of standing dead trees in the plot and record their diameter and decay class.
I calibrate the drone's camera before flying a grid pattern over the regeneration area to assess seedling survival.
